answers.say: I'm Alok, eighteen, from Uttarkashi, now a first-year Computer Science student at Newton School of Technology in Pune. I started with chess as a kid, picked up Java in Class nine, and now I build small tools and hackathon projects. This portfolio is the story, told out loud.

keys: why do you want to join
answers.say: Because Wispr Flow is building the future of voice, and I believe in it. I want to learn how to build products people love. I even steered this whole portfolio by voice, so it felt like the right place to say it.

This year I was recommended at the 1 AFSB in Dehradun on my first attempt, then ruled out at the medical stage because of a health issue. It hurt. But it pushed me to rebuild my plan, and that road led me to Newton School and to building things.

Bug Slayer, built with two teammates at the Hacktoberfest hackathon at NST. It reads a project's README, runs the setup in a Docker sandbox, and when something breaks it uses Gemma to diagnose the error and patch the lines. Seeing it fix a broken setup on its own felt great.

Bug Slayer is a Python command line tool. It runs the setup steps from a project's README inside a Docker sandbox. When a step fails, it asks Gemma to diagnose the failure and then patches the broken lines, and tries again.
Python and Java mostly, plus Git, and I edit videos too. I also contribute to open source, and I submit an alpha on WorldQuant BRAIN every day to keep my problem solving sharp.
Basketball and chess taught me to stay calm and think a move ahead. I break the problem into small steps, and I keep playing even when the score is against me. Hackathons are a good example of that.

I enjoy it. Bug Slayer was built with two teammates, and my Scratchathon team made it into the final ten out of eighty. I like agreeing on a plan quickly, sharing the load, and being honest when something is not working.

At Newton School I'm deepening Computer Science fundamentals, and building projects like CampusCompass, a campus navigation app. I'm also working toward Google Summer of Code, so open source is a big part of how I learn.

Something that fills a real gap in the apps and tools people use every day. I don't have the final idea yet, but I'm collecting those small frustrations, and voice is a big part of how I think products should feel.

I learn fast, I ship things, and I stay calm when plans change. I'm eighteen, hungry to build products people love, and I'll work hard to earn the chance. This portfolio is a small proof of how I work.

Chess, sudoku, video editing and basketball. I play power forward and center. I've played state level and inter-school games, won the CBSE cluster tournament, and played at the CBSE Nationals for Asian School.
